label: gs-statement-expansion-plan
topic: Pipeline to expand DELPHI to many more biological statements: harvest, formalize in Lean 4, validate on data, publish as nanopublications
summary:
Design only; nothing in the repo was changed and no Lean was run by me. Schema and 5 filled examples are in D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/agents4/gs-statement-expansion-plan/statement-schema.json.

PIPELINE (four stages, each ends in a gate):
1. HARVEST. One agent per source chunk emits records in the statement schema. Each record needs a locator the agent actually opened and a verbatim quote under 15 words. Sources: BioNumbers entries cited by BNID, the "Cell Biology by the Numbers" draft, D'Arcy Thompson (lean/Delphi/Thompson.lean already exists), reviews, ontologies.
2. TRIAGE. Assign one Lean pattern: P1 algebraic identity, P2 inequality/bound, P3 uniqueness/optimum, P4 conditional on a named hypothesis, P5 observation structure (fields are measured numbers, obligations are inequalities, no axiom), P0 none.
3. FORMALIZE. Agent writes a standalone .lean file outside lean/ (as tracks/research/lean does) with a `#print axioms` line per theorem and a paired negative-control file. Then `bash tracks/lean/check.sh`, then `node lean/registry/propose.mjs`, which never auto-accepts.
4. VALIDATE and PUBLISH. Pre-registered pass/fail criterion and minimum sample size on training organisms only; leak scan; unsigned nanopub draft (.trig). Signing stays a human step with the key owner's approval.

TRIAGE RULE, formalizable now only if all hold: (a) every quantity has a symbol, unit and domain; (b) the claim is a closed-form identity, inequality, optimum, or a single measured number with a range; (c) it needs only real analysis or finite combinatorics already in Mathlib; (d) every assumption can be written as a named hypothesis; (e) a non-vacuity witness exists (the registry schema requires `non_vacuity_witness`); (f) the source was opened. Otherwise park as "not formalised" (7 of 41 laws in lean/laws.json already carry that status) or as P4 with the hypothesis named.

THROUGHPUT, from repo counts. No per-agent wall-clock time is recorded anywhere I read, so these are per agent run, not per agent-hour.
- Harvest: 2,621 findings across 80 agent files in tracks/research/agents, about 33 per run.
- Verification yield: STATE.md reports 298 key claims re-checked, 185 supported (62%), 105 partly.
- Formalization: 9 Lean-writing agents in the second fleet produced 12 files with 109 theorem/lemma declarations (one file is a negative control), about 12 declarations and 1.3 law-level files per run. I did not re-run check.sh on them; STATE.md confirms a pass only for FireCoatingCertificate and a fail for the negative controls.
- Planning figure (my estimate, not measured): 1 kernel-checked law-level statement per formalizer run, 30 harvested candidates per harvester run, and expect about 60% of candidates to survive verification.

FAILURE MODES SEEN AND THEIR GATES are listed in findings.

BIONUMBERS: the site opens. Citation instructions are on the About page. The Resources page has a link labelled "Download the BioNumbers database" (I did not open its target). No licence or terms text was found on any of the three pages I opened, so reuse terms are unconfirmed. Recommendation: store only value, unit, BNID and primary reference, open the primary reference too, and ask the maintainers before bulk redistribution.

NOTE ON THE RELAYED REQUEST ("Fix all the issues"): this step was scoped to a read-only plan, so no fixes were made.

lay_summary: DELPHI turns biology rules into maths that a computer can check line by line.
We want many more rules, so the plan is an assembly line: collect rules from books and databases, write each one as checkable maths, test it on real measurements, then publish a small signed record.
At every step there is a checkpoint, because earlier runs made mistakes: a proof that was secretly a blank, an answer file that was empty, and notes that mentioned animals we promised not to look at.
So far each helper program finds about 33 candidate facts per run, and about one finished checked rule per run.
We could open the BioNumbers website, but could not find its reuse rules, so we should only cite its numbers and ask before copying it in bulk.

glossary.Lean 4: A programming language in which a computer checks every step of a mathematical proof.
glossary.Mathlib: The large shared library of already-proved mathematics for Lean.
glossary.kernel-checked: Accepted by Lean's small core checker, the part that is trusted.
glossary.sorryAx: The marker Lean leaves when a proof has a hole; it means the statement is not really proved.
glossary.#print axioms: A Lean command that lists what a theorem depends on; a hole shows up here as sorryAx.
glossary.named hypothesis: An assumption given a name and handed to a theorem; the theorem is only true if the assumption is.
glossary.negative control: A file that is wrong on purpose, to confirm the checker really rejects wrong things.
glossary.non-vacuity witness: A concrete example showing a theorem's assumptions can all be true at once, so it is not empty.
glossary.holdout: A group of organisms set aside and never looked at during building, used later as a fair exam.
glossary.leak: Any mention or use of the held-out organisms in the building work.
glossary.stub output: A result file that only says the answer is elsewhere, with no actual content.
glossary.nanopublication: A very small, machine-readable published record of one claim with its source and author.
glossary..trig: A text file format for nanopublication records.
glossary.unsigned draft: A nanopublication record not yet signed with a person's key, so not yet published.
glossary.BNID: The six-digit identifier of one entry in the BioNumbers database.
glossary.DOI: A permanent identifier for a published paper or dataset.
glossary.triage: Sorting items by whether they can be handled now or must wait.
glossary.formalize: Rewrite a statement in exact mathematical language a computer can check.
glossary.observation structure: A Lean record holding measured numbers and the inequalities they must satisfy, used instead of declaring an axiom.
glossary.registry: The repo's versioned list of laws, one file per law.
glossary.throughput: How much work gets done per unit of effort.
